milestone: 70S Ribosome Finite-State Tape Transducer
representative_system: Escherichia coli / LUCA 70S Ribosome
substrate_medium: 2.5-MDa ribonucleoprotein machine + mRNA / aminoacyl-tRNA
local_rule_or_gate: 64-codon -> 20-amino-acid + stop lookup table with EF-Tu GTP proofreading
computational_class: Finite-state tape transducer (programmable protein constructor)
plain_title: The ribosome reads three-letter mRNA words like a tape head
plain_text: Stepping three RNA letters at a time without slipping frames, each ribosome decodes 64 codons into 20 amino acids at ~18 peptide bonds a second—running ~20,000 tape heads in parallel inside one fast-growing bacterium.
source: Crick et al. (1961) Nature 192:1227; Ramakrishnan (2002) Cell 108:557; Milo & Phillips (2015) Cell Biology by the Numbers
note: Consumes ~4 high-energy phosphate bonds (~4 ATP-equivalents ≈ 3.8e-19 J) per amino acid incorporated, ~132× the 300 K Landauer floor.

milestone: DNA Polymerase III Hopfield-Ninio Kinetic Proofreading Head
representative_system: Escherichia coli Replisome (Pol III + Mismatch Repair)
substrate_medium: Duplex B-DNA template + dNTP triphosphates + exonuclease clamp
local_rule_or_gate: Two-stage irreversible pyrophosphate / exonuclease error-ratchet
computational_class: Thermodynamic error-correcting tape copier (~20× Landauer floor)
plain_title: DNA copying spends extra fuel to catch 99.99999998% of typos
plain_text: Thermal chemical binding alone would mispair roughly 1 in 10,000 DNA letters; by burning pyrophosphate to double-check every base and snipping out mismatches, bacterial DNA polymerase copies 1,000 letters a second at just ~20 times physics's minimum heat cost.
source: Hopfield (1974) PNAS 71:4135; Ninio (1975) Biochimie 57:587; Lee et al. (2012) PNAS 109:E2774
note: Matches canonical hardware benchmark row (5.7e-20 J/nucleotide ≈ 19.9 k_B T ln 2 at 300 K; in-vivo Pol III fork speed is ~750–1,000 nt/s).

milestone: Cis-Regulatory Promoter Boolean Logic (lac AND-NOT Gate)
representative_system: Escherichia coli lacZYA Operon (LacI + CRP-cAMP)
substrate_medium: Operator DNA + allosteric LacI tetramer + CRP-cAMP activator
local_rule_or_gate: Output = (Lactose / Allolactose) AND NOT (Glucose)
computational_class: Combinational Boolean logic gate & bistable hysteretic switch
plain_title: Gene switches wire IF-AND-NOT logic directly onto DNA
plain_text: E. coli turns on its milk-sugar genes IF lactose is present AND glucose is absent: a physical repressor blocks the DNA track until lactose pulls it off, while a second protein recruits RNA polymerase only when glucose runs low.
source: Jacob & Monod (1961) J. Mol. Biol. 3:318; Setty et al. (2003) PNAS 100:7702; Ozbudak et al. (2004) Nature 427:737
note: Across ~4,300 E. coli genes, ~300 transcription factors wire thousands of promoter logic gates (AND, OR, NAND, IMPLIES, feed-forward loops).

milestone: Tandem Riboswitch Allosteric mRNA Boolean Gate
representative_system: Vibrio cholerae gcvT Tandem Glycine Riboswitch / glmS Ribozyme
substrate_medium: 5'-untranslated mRNA aptamer folds (zero protein transcription factors)
local_rule_or_gate: Cooperative two-aptamer glycine AND gate / self-cleaving NOR gate
computational_class: Protein-free single-molecule RNA Boolean logic gate
plain_title: Messenger RNA folds itself into logic gates without any proteins
plain_text: Before a ribosome even starts translating, structured RNA pockets directly grab small metabolites like glycine or vitamin B12 and snap into a new 3D fold that flips gene expression on or off.
source: Mandal et al. (2004) Science 306:275; Sudarsan et al. (2006) Science 314:300; Breaker (2012) Cold Spring Harb. Perspect. Biol. 4:a003566
note: Demonstrates relics of RNA-world molecular computation still operating across modern bacterial genomes.

milestone: CRISPR-Cas1-Cas2 Chronological Genomic Push-Down Stack
representative_system: Streptococcus / Escherichia coli CRISPR-Cas Spacer Array
substrate_medium: Chromosomal repeat-spacer DNA locus + Cas1-Cas2 integrase + crRNA
local_rule_or_gate: Leader-proximal LIFO DNA write + sequence-matched Cas endonuclease cut
computational_class: Chronological write-once genomic tape recorder & pattern matcher
plain_title: Bacteria splice viral mugshots onto a time-ordered DNA tape
plain_text: Cas1-Cas2 enzymes snip 33-letter DNA fragments from invading viruses and always paste the newest spacer at the front of the CRISPR array—creating a chronological genomic logbook that Shipman & Church later harnessed to record a digital movie into living E. coli.
source: Barrangou et al. (2007) Science 315:1709; Yosef et al. (2012) Nucleic Acids Res. 40:5569; Shipman et al. (2017) Nature 547:345
note: Each 33-bp protospacer stores 66 bits in strict arrival order; Cas9/Cas12 R-loop interrogation scans ~30–100 target sites/s inside a cell.

milestone: Diversity-Generating Retroelement (DGR) Targeted Adenine Mutator
representative_system: Bordetella phage BPP-1 Diversity-Generating Retroelement
substrate_medium: Template repeat RNA + error-prone reverse transcriptase (bRT) + Avd
local_rule_or_gate: Selective A -> {A,C,G,T} rewrite at 23 target codons while preserving scaffold
computational_class: Targeted combinatorial Monte Carlo sequence generator (10^14–10^20 variants)
plain_title: Viruses and microbes randomize only chosen DNA letters across 10¹⁴–10²⁰ keys
plain_text: Instead of mutating its whole genome at random, a reverse-transcriptase enzyme copies a clean template RNA and deliberately scrambles only adenine letters inside the tail-fiber binding tip—exploring up to 10²⁰ protein keys while keeping the structural frame intact.
source: Liu et al. (2002) Science 295:2091; Doulatov et al. (2004) Nature 431:476; Roux et al. (2021) Nat. Microbiol. 6:499
note: Here high per-adenine substitution (~75% non-A incorporation at targeted TR adenines) is the computational randomization primitive rather than an unintended error.

milestone: RNA-Guided Scrambled Genome Compiler (225,000 DNA Segments)
representative_system: Oxytricha trifallax Germline-to-Somatic Genome Unscrambler
substrate_medium: Micronuclear scrambled MDS segments + maternal template RNAs + PiggyMac
local_rule_or_gate: Pointer-guided DNA deletion, inversion & permutation into 16,000 nanochromosomes
computational_class: Pointer-linked graph-rewriting DNA compiler
plain_title: A single-celled ciliate unscrambles 225,000 shuffled DNA pieces using RNA maps
plain_text: Oxytricha stores its silent germline genome as 225,000 out-of-order, upside-down DNA fragments; after mating, it deletes 90% of its DNA and uses long RNA templates from its parents to stitch the fragments back into ~16,000 working single-gene chromosomes.
source: Landweber et al. (2000) PNAS 97:3298; Swart et al. (2013) PLoS Biol. 11:e1001473; Chen et al. (2014) Cell 158:1187
note: Inspires formal pointer-guided DNA recombination models proved Turing-universal by Ehrenfeucht, Prescott & Rozenberg (2003) and Kari & Landweber.

milestone: Somatic V(D)J Recombination & Hypermutation Immune Search
representative_system: Jawed-Vertebrate B/T Lymphocyte Repertoire (RAG1/2 + AID)
substrate_medium: Chromosomal V, D, J gene cassettes + RAG1/2 recombinase + TdT
local_rule_or_gate: 12/23-bp spacer rule cut-and-join + N-nucleotide junctional entropy + clonal selection
computational_class: Distributed somatic evolutionary search (~10^11 parallel lymphocyte agents)
plain_title: Vertebrate white blood cells edit their own DNA into billions of antigen keys
plain_text: Each developing B and T cell physically cuts and splices V, D and J gene blocks—tossing random DNA letters into the joints—so one human body runs ~10¹¹ distinct receptor guesses in parallel against pathogens that have not even evolved yet.
source: Tonegawa (1983) Nature 302:575; Schatz et al. (1989) Cell 59:1035; Flajnik & Kasahara (2010) Nat. Rev. Genet. 11:47
note: ~2/3 of out-of-frame junctions trigger backup allele rearrangement or apoptosis, trading cell-level waste for >10^11 repertoire diversity.

milestone: Turing Reaction-Diffusion Morphogen Lattice
representative_system: Vertebrate / Metazoan Epithelial Activator-Inhibitor Field (Nodal-Lefty / Wnt-Dkk)
substrate_medium: 2D embryonic cell sheet + short-range activator & fast-diffusing inhibitor
local_rule_or_gate: du/dt = f(u,v) + D_u ∇²u, dv/dt = g(u,v) + D_v ∇²v (D_v >> D_u)
computational_class: Continuous-state 2D spatial symmetry-breaking field
plain_title: Local activate-near, inhibit-far rules paint stripes, spots and fingers
plain_text: Alan Turing showed in 1952 that a uniform sheet of cells with no central blueprint spontaneously breaks symmetry into periodic stripes, spots and digit spacing whenever a slow local activator triggers a faster-spreading inhibitor.
source: Turing (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37; Kondo & Miura (2010) Science 329:1616; Raspopovic et al. (2014) Science 345:566
note: Continuous partial-differential precursor that coarse-grains directly into discrete cellular automata when tissue geometry compartmentalizes diffusion.

milestone: 1D Mantle-Edge Shell Pigment Automaton (Rule-30 Analogue)
representative_system: Conus textile & Oliva porphyria Marine Gastropod Mantle Margin
substrate_medium: 1D line of neurosecretory & pigment cells along growing CaCO3 shell lip
local_rule_or_gate: 1D lateral-inhibition excitability wave recorded row-by-row into calcified shell
computational_class: Living 1D space-time cellular automaton (Class 3 aperiodic triangles)
plain_title: A cone snail prints a 1D Wolfram Rule-30 pattern onto its growing shell
plain_text: A narrow row of pigment cells along the lip of Conus textile only senses its immediate left and right neighbors; as the shell grows forward day by day, it freezes time into space, printing the same chaotic nested triangles generated by Wolfram's Rule 30.
source: Meinhardt (1995) The Algorithmic Beauty of Sea Shells; Coombes et al. (2009) PNAS 106:8429; Wolfram (2002) A New Kind of Science p. 423
note: Conidae fossil shells appear in Early Eocene strata (~55 Ma); whole snail CNS (~200,000 neurons) runs ~4e6 synaptic ops/s while the mantle lip logs ~0.55 pigment updates/s.

milestone: Discrete 2D Skin-Scale Cellular Automaton
representative_system: Timon lepidus (Ocellated Lizard) Hexagonal Skin-Scale Lattice
substrate_medium: 2D hexagonal lattice of ~5,000 thick keratinized scales separated by thin borders
local_rule_or_gate: Discrete 6-neighbor green/black color-flipping rule (~3–4 green neighbors -> black)
computational_class: Experimentally verified living 2D discrete von Neumann/hexagonal CA
plain_title: Lizard scales flip green or black by counting their six neighbors—a real 2D cellular automaton
plain_text: In 2017, time-lapse tracking of thousands of individual scales on growing ocellated lizards proved that thin borders between scales discretize Turing's reaction-diffusion equations into a literal 2D cellular automaton where single scales flip between green and black from neighbor counts.
source: Manukyan, Montandon, Fofonjka, Smirnov & Milinkovitch (2017) Nature 544:173
note: First rigorous mathematical derivation and longitudinal multi-year in-vivo verification of a discrete 2D cellular automaton in a living vertebrate.

milestone: Von Neumann 29-State Self-Reproducing Universal Constructor CA
representative_system: Von Neumann 2D 5-Neighbor 29-State Cellular Automaton (~200,000 cells)
substrate_medium: 2D orthogonal grid (5-cell von Neumann neighborhood, 29 states/cell)
local_rule_or_gate: Signal-wire transmission + confluent/unexcited logic + construction arm
computational_class: Turing-universal + constructor-universal (open-ended self-reproduction)
plain_title: Von Neumann proves self-reproduction needs both a passive tape and an active builder
plain_text: Five years before Watson and Crick solved DNA's double helix, John von Neumann designed a 29-state cellular grid machine that copies its own 1D instruction tape uninterpreted and executes it to build a complete daughter machine—predicting life's DNA-plus-ribosome split from pure logic.
source: von Neumann (1948) Hixon Symposium; von Neumann & Burks (1966) Theory of Self-Reproducing Automata; Pesavento (1995) Complex Systems 9:333
note: Hardware step latency & energy shown for modern silicon emulation of the 200,000-cell configuration.

milestone: Conway's Game of Life 2D Outer-Totalistic Automaton (B3/S23)
representative_system: Conway Game of Life (2D Moore Neighborhood, 2 States)
substrate_medium: 2D 8-neighbor binary grid (glider guns, Logic gates & 0E0P metacells)
local_rule_or_gate: Birth on 3 live neighbors; survival on 2 or 3 live neighbors (B3/S23)
computational_class: Turing-universal + universal self-reproducing constructor (Gemini / 0E0P)
plain_title: Two states and two counting rules spawn gliders, logic gates and self-copying machines
plain_text: John Conway's 1970 two-rule grid ('born with 3 neighbors, survive with 2 or 3') proved that dead-simple local arithmetic generates gliders, memory registers, universal computers, and even huge patterns that construct full copies of themselves.
source: Gardner (1970) Sci. Am. 223(4):120; Berlekamp, Conway & Guy (1982) Winning Ways; Rendell (2002) Collision-Based Computing
note: Historical 1970 mainframe/minicomputer rate ~2.5e6 cell updates/s; modern Hashlife/GPU implementations exceed 10^12 cell-generations/s.

milestone: Wolfram Elementary Rule 30 Chaotic Cryptographic Automaton
representative_system: Wolfram 1D Elementary Cellular Automaton Rule 30 (00011110_2)
substrate_medium: 1D binary array (3-cell neighborhood: left, center, right)
local_rule_or_gate: next(C) = L XOR (C OR R)  [8-bit truth table 00011110_2 = 30]
computational_class: Wolfram Class 3 chaotic / computationally irreducible PRNG
plain_title: One tiny rule—L XOR (C OR R)—turns a single dot into inexhaustible randomness
plain_text: Starting from a single black cell on a blank row, Wolfram's Rule 30 produces a center column so statistically random it served for years as Mathematica's random-number generator—showing that deterministic physics needs no external noise to look chaotic.
source: Wolfram (1983) Rev. Mod. Phys. 55:601; Wolfram (1986) Adv. Appl. Math. 7:123; Wolfram (2002) A New Kind of Science
note: Illustrates computational irreducibility: no known closed-form shortcut predicts the n-th center bit markedly faster than running n steps.

milestone: Wolfram-Cook Elementary Rule 110 Universal Cellular Automaton
representative_system: Wolfram 1D Elementary Cellular Automaton Rule 110 (01101110_2)
substrate_medium: 1D binary array (3-cell neighborhood, 2 states, 8-bit rule table)
local_rule_or_gate: next(C) = (C OR R) AND NOT (L AND C AND R)  [01101110_2 = 110]
computational_class: Wolfram Class 4 localized-glider Turing-universal cellular automaton
plain_title: Rule 110 proves 1D 2-state local neighbors are already a universal Turing computer
plain_text: Conjectured by Stephen Wolfram and proved by Matthew Cook (2004), Rule 110 sits on the knife-edge between order and chaos: stable repeating background tiles support colliding 'spaceship' gliders that emulate cyclic tag systems and therefore any possible computer program.
source: Cook (2004) Complex Systems 15:1; Wolfram (2002) A New Kind of Science Ch. 11; Neary & Woods (2006) MFCS 4162:742
note: Neary & Woods (2006) further proved Rule 110 simulates Turing machines with only polynomial time overhead (P-complete prediction).

milestone: Minimal (2,3) Universal Turing Machine & BFF Self-Replicating Tape Soup
representative_system: Wolfram-Smith 2-State 3-Symbol UTM (2007) & Agüera y Arcas BFF Soup (2024)
substrate_medium: 1D symbolic tape + minimal finite-state head / self-modifying byte tapes
local_rule_or_gate: 6-transition (2-state, 3-color) head rule; random 64-byte BFF tape collisions
computational_class: Minimal-state universal Turing machine & spontaneous replicator emergence
plain_title: Universal computation needs just 2 states and 3 symbols—and unseeded tapes self-replicate
plain_text: Alex Smith proved in 2007 that a 2-state, 3-symbol Turing machine is already universal; in 2024 Agüera y Arcas and colleagues showed that random Brainfuck-like tapes colliding with zero fitness function abruptly snap into self-copying replicators.
source: Smith (2007) Complex Systems 29:1; Wolfram (2002) p. 709; Agüera y Arcas et al. (2024) arXiv:2406.19108
note: Separates two thresholds: Turing universality is ubiquitous even in 6-rule systems, whereas open-ended replication requires self-copying tape closure.

category: 4. Engineered DNA Computers & DNA Tile Automata
milestone: Adleman Combinatorial DNA Hamiltonian-Path Computer
representative_system: Adleman 7-City Directed Hamiltonian Path Oligonucleotide Pool (1994)
substrate_medium: 20-mer ssDNA city/edge strands + T4 DNA ligase + PCR + magnetic beads
local_rule_or_gate: Watson-Crick 10-bp half-city hybridization + enzymatic ligation & affinity sieve
computational_class: Massively parallel combinatorial NP-path filter (~3×10^13 molecules)
plain_title: Leonard Adleman solves a 7-city travel puzzle inside a drop of DNA
plain_text: In 1994 Leonard Adleman encoded cities and one-way flights as 20-letter DNA strands; shaken together in 50 microlitres of water, ~30 trillion molecules explored candidate routes at once via base pairing while gels and magnetic beads filtered out the exact 7-city tour.
source: Adleman (1994) Science 266:1021
note: ~10^20 J⁻¹ ligation efficiency during hybridization, though human wet-lab sieving took 7 days and brute-force NP molecular volume scales exponentially with graph size.

category: 4. Engineered DNA Computers & DNA Tile Automata
milestone: Autonomous Enzyme-Powered DNA Finite Automaton
representative_system: Benenson-Shapiro FokI Restriction-Nuclease Autonomous DNA Automaton (2001)
substrate_medium: dsDNA input tape + transition dsDNA molecules + FokI nuclease + T4 ligase + ATP
local_rule_or_gate: 4-nt sticky-end state encoding; FokI cleaves offset downstream to expose next state
computational_class: Autonomous 2-state finite-state automaton (~10^12 parallel machines/droplet)
plain_title: A trillion autonomous DNA state machines run in one microlitre with zero human steps
plain_text: Ehud Shapiro's team built a complete finite-state machine out of DNA, ATP and the scissor enzyme FokI that steps down a DNA input molecule on its own—later extended to sense mRNA disease markers and release a drug strand only when IF-AND-NOT conditions hold.
source: Benenson, Paz-Elizur, Adar, Keinan, Livneh & Shapiro (2001) Nature 414:430; Benenson et al. (2004) Nature 429:423
note: Measured ~10^9 state transitions/s across a ~10 µL reaction (~5×10^-8 W chemical dissipation, ~35× Landauer floor).

category: 4. Engineered DNA Computers & DNA Tile Automata
milestone: Self-Assembling DNA Tile Cellular Automaton (Wolfram Rule 90 Sierpiński XOR)
representative_system: Rothemund-Papadakis-Winfree DX DNA Tile Rule-90 Ribbon Crystal (2004)
substrate_medium: Double-crossover (DX) DNA tiles with four 5-nt programmable sticky ends
local_rule_or_gate: 2-input sticky-end binding executes Rule 90: out = left XOR right (Sierpiński gasket)
computational_class: Algorithmic self-assembling 1D cellular automaton (Winfree universal aTAM class)
plain_title: DNA tiles snap together by sticky ends to grow a physical Wolfram cellular automaton
plain_text: Erik Winfree proved that 2D crystal growth is equivalent to cellular-automaton computation; in 2004 Paul Rothemund, Nick Papadakis and Winfree designed four DNA tiles whose sticky ends compute XOR, self-assembling nanoscale Sierpiński-triangle crystals visible under atomic-force microscopy.
source: Winfree (1998) Caltech PhD Thesis; Rothemund, Papadakis & Winfree (2004) PLoS Biol. 2:e424
note: Direct physical bridge between Wolfram's 1D cellular automata and DNA base-pairing: crystal growth axis = time t, tile row = spatial state x, mismatch error 0.14%–1.4%.

category: 4. Engineered DNA Computers & DNA Tile Automata
milestone: Toehold Seesaw DNA Strand-Displacement Digital & Neural Circuits
representative_system: Qian-Winfree 130-Strand 4-Bit Square-Root Circuit (2011) & Cherry-Qian Winner-Take-All Net (2018)
substrate_medium: Enzyme-free synthetic ssDNA/dsDNA toehold seesaw gates in buffer
local_rule_or_gate: Reversible toehold branch migration OR/AND/NOT + linear threshold weight sum
computational_class: Scalable enzyme-free Boolean & analog neural-network wetware
plain_title: Enzyme-free DNA strand swaps compute square roots and recognize handwritten digits
plain_text: Lulu Qian and Erik Winfree wired 130 synthetic DNA strands into seesaw logic gates that compute 4-bit square roots purely by base-pair branch migration—and in 2018 Kevin Cherry and Qian scaled the same gates to classify 100-bit handwritten numbers in a test tube.
source: Qian & Winfree (2011) Science 332:1196; Qian, Winfree & Bruck (2011) Nature 475:368; Cherry & Qian (2018) Nature 559:370
note: Matches canonical hardware benchmark row (1,100 s diffusive cascade latency, 5.0e-19 J/op = 2.0e18 Ops/J, ~174× Landauer floor).

category: 4. Engineered DNA Computers & DNA Tile Automata
milestone: Reprogrammable 355-Tile 6-Bit DNA Cellular-Automaton Circuit Family
representative_system: Woods-Doty-Myhrvold-Winfree 355-Tile Programmable DNA Nanotube Automaton (2019)
substrate_medium: 355 single-stranded DNA tiles self-assembling into 16-helix nanotubes
local_rule_or_gate: 6-bit iterative Boolean/CA layer running 21 algorithms (Rule 110, leader election, sorting, parity, RNG)
computational_class: Field-reprogrammable algorithmic DNA tile cellular automaton
plain_title: One library of 355 DNA tiles runs 21 programs—including Wolfram's universal Rule 110
plain_text: Damien Woods, David Doty, Cameron Myhrvold and Erik Winfree built a universal 355-strand DNA tile set where picking a subset of strands programs growing DNA nanotubes to execute copying, sorting, palindromes, random walks, and Wolfram's Rule 110 at <0.03% per-tile error.
source: Woods, Doty, Myhrvold, Hui, Zhou, Yin & Winfree (2019) Nature 567:366
note: Landmark experimental unification of reprogrammable digital gate arrays, DNA self-assembly, and Wolfram Rule 110 cellular automata.

category: 4. Engineered DNA Computers & DNA Tile Automata
milestone: General-Purpose DNA-Based Programmable Gate Array (DPGA)
representative_system: Lv-Wang-Zhu-Fan 24-Gate Reconfigurable DNA Integrated Circuit (2023)
substrate_medium: DNA origami wiring + dual-rail seesaw strand-displacement gates (~500 strands)
local_rule_or_gate: Oligonucleotide instruction-wired universal NOR/OR/AND network (>100 billion circuits)
computational_class: Liquid-phase general-purpose reprogrammable molecular IC
plain_title: Liquid-phase DNA field-programmable gate arrays wire over 100 billion possible circuits
plain_text: By standardizing DNA strand-displacement gates with DNA-origami signal transmission so any circuit can be wired with short instruction strands without redesigning molecules from scratch, researchers demonstrated multi-layer 500-strand DNA circuits solving quadratic equations and classifying microRNAs.
source: Lv, Wang, Zhu, Dong, Zhang, Li & Fan (2023) Nature 622:292
note: Demonstrates multi-DPGA cascading with minimal signal attenuation across 3 layers and ~30 logic gates.
